bipartite.kami_theme: The tangled, disordered pattern of Shinobu-dyed cloth from Michinoku — a fixed image of chaotic interwoven lines used here as jokotoba/simile
bipartite.shimo_theme: The speaker's own heart thrown into disordered longing, and the question of whose fault (whose love) has caused this — protesting that it is not the speaker's own doing
bipartite.pivot_note: The kami-no-ku describes the visually tangled, irregular dye-pattern of shinobu-zuri cloth; this physical image of 'midare' (disarray) is not stated as metaphor but functions as a jokotoba that phonetically and semantically slides into the shimo's midare-someni-shi (my heart has become disordered/dyed with longing) — the cloth's random tangled pattern IS the speaker's tangled heart, the comparison implicit rather than declared with 'like' or 'as'.

kigo.note: Shinobu-zuri is a famous textile/place-name image (Michinoku) but carries no seasonal marker — it functions as a conventional utamakura (poetic place-name) evoking rustic disorder and longing rather than season. No true kigo is present in this poem; the imagery is textile/emotional, not seasonal.

kakekotoba.reading_primary: しのぶ (place name / cloth type, Shinobu-zuri)
kakekotoba.reading_secondary: 忍ぶ (to endure secretly, to conceal one's love)
kakekotoba.interaction: The word names the specific tangled-dye cloth of the Shinobu district while simultaneously invoking 'to endure/conceal' — suggesting the speaker's secret, endured love that has now broken into visible disorder, paralleling the cloth's chaotic pattern becoming a public sign of hidden feeling made manifest.

kakekotoba.reading_primary: 乱れ初めにし (began to become disordered)
kakekotoba.reading_secondary: 乱れ染めにし (became disordered/dyed, echoing the dyeing of the cloth)
kakekotoba.interaction: そめ operates as a pivot between 初め (began) and 染め (dyed), linking the onset of the speaker's emotional disarray to the physical dyeing process of the shinobu-zuri cloth introduced in the kami-no-ku, fusing the jokotoba's textile imagery with the shimo's confession of unbidden passion.

jokotoba.text: みちのくの しのぶもぢずり
jokotoba.pivot: 乱れ (disorder) — the tangled dye-pattern of shinobu-zuri cloth introduces the idea of 'midare' which is then applied to the speaker's heart
jokotoba.function: Establishes an extended, freely composed (not fixed) image of the famous Michinoku shinobu-zuri cloth, whose randomly tangled dye pattern serves as the vehicle that leads, via the shared idea of 'midare' (disarray), into the shimo-no-ku's description of the speaker's heart thrown into confused longing.

source_jp:
みちのくの
しのぶもぢずり
誰故に
乱れそめにし
我ならなくに
